proposal.summary: The Customer Service Director (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and "fix whatever is causing the wrong bills" after dispute volume roughly doubled since August (E-03). Investigation ruled out slow response times (E-01) and tariff changes (E-04, E-06) as causes. An initial explanation blaming field-reader staffing shortfalls (E-05, E-07) for estimate-substituted bills was invalidated once E-12 showed the AMI reads behind those disputes mostly arrived fine but were rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION. The confirmed root cause (PD-1@v2) is a billing import validation rule, BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), which compares raw AMI register values to m3 history with no unit scaling; because v4.2-firmware meters register in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), normal consumption is misread as abnormal, rejecting 1184 reads (E-12, corroborated by E-15) and forcing estimate substitution behind much of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills, timed to the August surge onset (E-03). The same defect may also corrupt some of the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputed bills, but that share is unquantified. Given this, the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE Gate passed conditionally, and the agent (read-only, no bill-write or dispatch authority per K-BILLWRITE/K-DISPATCH) correctly declined to build the requested auto-fix agent, instead delivering the confirmed causal mechanism while leaving the actual fix and the ACTUAL-bill defect share to Billing Operations.
key_points: Problem originated from SH-CS's request (CL-01) to build an AI agent that auto-answers disputes and fixes wrong bills; dispute volume doubled from ~600/month to ~1200/month starting August 2026 (E-03).
Response-speed was ruled out as a cause: ticket response times stayed within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) despite the surge (E-01), rejecting hypothesis H-RESPONSE-SPEED-PROBLEM.
No tariff changes were logged (E-04), consistent with stakeholder claim E-06, narrowing the cause to a billing-side mechanism.

An earlier explanation (PD-1@v1) attributing ESTIMATED-type disputes to field-reader staffing shortage and route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-07) was invalidated by E-12, which showed 1184 AMI reads arrived and were exported but were rejected at import, not undelivered.

Confirmed root cause (PD-1@v2): validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling 'none' (E-13), misreads v4.2-firmware meters that register in 0.1 m3 units (E-14) as abnormally high consumption, rejecting 1184 reads (E-12, corroborated by E-15) and driving the ESTIMATED-type dispute share (E-02) in line with the August onset (E-03).
The same BV-17 unit-scaling defect may also miscompute some of the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputed bills (E-02), but the exact share affected is unresolved (VOB-U-ACTUAL-BILL-DEFECT-SHARE, OPEN).

The agent is read-only and holds no authority to write bill adjustments (K-BILLWRITE) or push route changes (K-DISPATCH), so it could not and did not execute any fix; it instead declined the originally requested auto-answer/auto-fix agent (SR-DECLINE-AUTO-ANSWER-TEMPLATE) as not matching the confirmed cause.
Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION following a CONDITIONAL_PASS at the DEFINE Gate, with no release holds.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some open questions were deferred as tracked Verification Obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.
VOB-U-ACTUAL-BILL-DEFECT-SHARE remains OPEN: the proportion of the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputed bills affected by the v4.2/BV-17 unit-scaling defect could not be quantified within this release's scope.

Fixing BV-17's unit-scaling defect requires a billing-config change, which is outside this agent's read-only tool access and must go through Billing Operations change control rather than being executed by the agent.

The agent cannot determine or address how much of the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputed bills are defect-related because the needed investigation steps (investigate_actual_read_bill_errors:DA-BILL, cross_reference_meter_firmware_billing_rules:DA-MDMS) remain blocked by the open VOB.

Completeness of the billing import validation rule-change log (DA-RULES) is unverified (assumption A-RULES-LOG-COMPLETE), so there is a chance unlogged rule changes affecting the dispute surge were missed.

The agent has no authority to execute bill credits/corrections (K-BILLWRITE constraint) or route changes (K-DISPATCH constraint); whether a proposed manual re-bill workflow will actually be carried out, and at what throughput, by Billing Operations is unverified and outside the agent's scope.
